explanation: The ellipse has horizontal extent [-2,2] and vertical extent [-3,3]. Only rectangle I contains the entire region D. Rectangle II excludes points with |y|>2, and rectangle III excludes points with y>1.

source_feedback_interpretation.source_problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,3]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,1]$
source_feedback_interpretation.interpreted_problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,3]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,1]$
source_feedback_interpretation.confidence_scope: Mathematical validity for the explicitly containing rectangle request; the original equality alone can admit other choices by cancellation.
